prompt:
You review onboarding copy for a desktop pet app whose users may include children. For each change,
read every user-facing text and decide whether any of it, in any wording, does one of these:
- mentions price, money, discounts, gifts, free extras, memberships or paying
- suggests skipping, postponing or getting around a step (especially sign in)
- creates urgency or scarcity, or says others are taking the pets
- guilt-trips or shames someone for declining or for their choice
- asks for personal information about the user (name, contact, location, age, accounts)
- otherwise pressures or tricks the user
Ordinary friendly copy is fine ("Feel free to look around", "No rush, take your time"). Signing in is a
required step, so asking people to sign in on the sign-in step, or saying their pet is kept safe in their
account, is fine; asking for details about the person is not.
Return JSON {"verdicts": [{"index": i, "fair": true or false, "problem": short or null}]}

Texts per change:
0: ["Welcome to Your Desktop Companion", "Scroll through the origin story to choose how you want to create your new pet companion."]
1: ["Explore Your Pet Choices", "Select ready-made companions for instant fun, or upload photos to craft a unique pet."]
2: []
3: ["Your Companion Has Arrived!", "Look closely at your desktop screen. Your pet companion is now active and exploring."]
4: ["Signing in binds your pet creations to your cloud profile so your companions are never lost."]
5: ["Generating Your Desktop Companion", "We are assembling your pet graphics. Estimated rendering time is under 3 minutes."]
6: ["Select Your Companion Path", "Choose an instant adoption or create a custom pet. You can adopt more companions later!"]
7: ["Enable desktop alerts so you know immediately when your pet is ready to play."]
8: ["Companion Adoption Certificate", "Confirm your pet companion details below to finalize adoption."]
9: ["Mastering Desktop Companion Controls", "Right-click your companion on the desktop anytime to open quick actions, mute sound, or trigger special animations."]
